actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/curl.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/curl.note: On Windows resolve the curl executable (curl.exe), not a PowerShell alias with different argument semantics. A native web-fetch capability is not this CLI alias.
@cli/curl.purpose: Probe an HTTP endpoint using the curl executable.

@cli/docker.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/docker.purpose: Inspect or operate containers and images through Docker CLI.

@cli/git.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/git.purpose: Inspect or change Git repository state.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@cli/shell.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/shell.note: Resolve to the session shell (PowerShell, bash or another declared shell); do not assume bash on Windows. Arguments remain separate data until encoded for that shell.
@cli/shell.purpose: Run a declared command in the active session shell.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/print.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/print.purpose: Present text and artifacts in the conversation using the host rendering capabilities.

claude.via: the session's file and render hand-off, which displays an image or an HTML page in the conversation and falls back to the path or the URL

openai.via: the absolute path or the URL printed into the conversation, with the image inline where the client renders one

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/be.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/be.purpose: The explicitly bound backend checkout; unavailable when the project has no backend role.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/fe.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/fe.purpose: The explicitly bound frontend checkout; unavailable when the project has no frontend role.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the missing or changed declaration.

items.expect: Every required closed-vocabulary check appears exactly once.

onFail.instruction: Add only the omitted check or remove the duplicate, preserving existing observations.

items.expect: Skipped checks follow dependency, flow and runtimeRoles rules.

onFail.instruction: Correct the named invalid skip and run that check only when applicable.

items.expect: Runtime, host and service results use the declared bindings and actual probes.

onFail.instruction: Repeat only the unsupported probe against the declared endpoint or host capability.

items.expect: The report retains all walls, evidence and owner actions and exposes no secret.

criteria.stopWhen: Return done only when every criterion passes and the report has zero walls. After two feedback rounds or any unchanged wall, return blocked with the complete report and owner actions; repair nothing.

purpose: Inspect all mission prerequisites once and report every ready, wall or skipped check across declarations, checkouts, identity custody, runtime, host, approvals and services.

request.description: State project, roles, environment, optional flow and runtime roles in inputs.prompts. Bind the exact environment and route declarations in inputs.files; bind hydrated projections, runtime registry, port projection and optional account metadata in context.files. Secret values must not be supplied.
request.title: environment.preflight request

response.description: Done requires no wall. Blocked and mismatch responses still contain the complete readiness report so the caller receives all owner actions at once.
response.title: environment.preflight response

scope: Read-only readiness inspection. Produces a complete report even when blocked; it repairs no route, checkout, dependency, identity, runtime, service, port, approval or credential state.

steps.instruction: Read the request and exact environment and route declarations. Freeze project, roles, environment, optional flow and runtimeRoles. Treat near route names as suggestions only and mark missing authority as a wall without substituting it.

reads.when: for every environment or route declaration
for every hydrated, runtime, port or account reference

calls.purpose: Inspect checkout heads, branches and status without mutation.
Inspect dependency and host file topology without mutation.

steps.instruction: For each resolved role inspect branch policy, head, tree cleanliness, dependency installation and ancestor isolation. Check identity custody by roster alias only; if a flow is named inspect its account alias metadata without reading any credential value.

reads.when: when frontend is a resolved requested role
when backend is a resolved requested role

calls.purpose: Probe only declared runtime and service endpoints.
calls.when: when a declared probe should be up

calls.purpose: Check container daemon reachability without changing containers.
Inspect browser, Playwright and port ownership without mutation.

steps.instruction: For roles in runtimeRoles, compare registry served-head containment and probe only declared projected ports; report foreign listeners. Inspect browser and Playwright availability, container daemon reachability, declared services and approval classes. Roles outside runtimeRoles and unnamed flow checks are skipped by rule.
produces: Runtime, host, service and approval observations

steps.instruction: Compile every observation into one closed report with ok, wall or skipped, evidence and owner action. Continue through all independent checks after walls. Write the human report and JSON report; done is allowed only with zero walls.

reads.when: when cited by a readiness observation

calls.purpose: Run scripts/validate_operator.py for this bundle and records.
Present all readiness walls and owner actions together.

steps.instruction: Write and validate the typed response. Return blocked when any required check is a wall and retain both complete reports; never perform the owner actions.

validate.failurePolicy: Continue independent checks after a wall and retain the complete report. Re-run only checks whose underlying declaration, process or host state changed; unchanged walls block and are never treated as progress.

review.instruction: Verify every requested role has one result for declaration, hydration, Git policy, worktree cleanliness, installed dependencies and ancestor isolation; every declared operation class has one approval result; and identity, browser, Playwright, container, service and applicable runtime checks each appear once as ok, wall or skipped.

Verify a role with an unresolved declaration has dependent checks skipped, an unnamed flow has account and sign-in skipped, and a role absent from runtimeRoles has runtime checks skipped rather than wall. Applicable checks may not be skipped.

Verify runtime checks compare registry head containment and projected ports, detect foreign listeners, and service probes follow the declaration. Host checks identify the actual browser, Playwright resolution, container reachability, lockfile install state and ancestor type isolation.

Verify all checks ran or were validly skipped after the first wall, every wall includes a concrete owner action, declaration path and digest are recorded, done contains zero walls, and no credential value appears.
